finding.summary: The pinned historical_source 50fc42f has Plan4c T10 without its review fixes: the six c1/c2/c3 commits on p4c-t10c (bf5593c, 451e934, 3ef0f23, 0afc8c8, e144f96, 358dac6) are not ancestors of it, so the pinned harness.py sha (ee90fa55…) is the pre-fix version.
finding.failure_scenario: Overlaying base..50fc42f lands a wsd/harness.py that logs the raw install name and the btq gap text, and may publish readouts it should refuse. Those are the security fixes T10 c1/c2/c3 made, so the integration silently regresses reviewed fixes. The single permitted final T10 review would then be spent on a candidate missing those rounds.

findings.response: Corrected T10 source and stale-aggregate exclusion are explicit; no missing security fixes may be selected.

finding.summary: 'Reconcile Plan4c T8/T9/T10 and T11' gets predecessor state wrong: p4c-t8 and p4c-t9 are already in the common base 2c0c5b5. p4c-t11 (8 commits) and p4c-t13 (12 commits) are not in the historical source at all. Only part of T10 (via p4c-t10b) is in it, and its latest work is on p4c-t10c.
finding.failure_scenario: A d2 author following this text treats T8/T9 as integration work and treats T11 as something the source-map delta contains. T11's documentation of T10's fixes and T13's live checks are then never mapped or admitted, or are assumed done because they are listed next to completed tasks.

findings.response: Separate already-landed ancestry, unfinished native predecessor state, and explicitly excluded T11/T13 ports.

finding.summary: The ADR applies a strict 'maximum three rounds per change' and 'old reviews do not reset the counter' (line 39), but never records Liam's authenticated choice A (Marmot ask xjgx). That choice allows exactly one final T10 review as a cap exception, and is neither deployment approval nor a blanket waiver.
finding.failure_scenario: T10 has already used rounds c1-c3. As written, the design either leaves T10 with no route to completion, or an executor uses the exception informally with nothing stating its bounds: one review, T10 only, which T10 (Plan4c, not plan5i-2 T10/T10b), and against which exact candidate. That invites a second exception round or treating it as approval to deploy.

findings.response: Retain actual authenticated xjgx one-review exception and remaining-blocker return rule.

finding.summary: The ADR says the full base-to-source delta must be mapped to original plans and actual review records before a landing sequence is chosen. The source map has only flat path lists, with no commit, task, plan or review mapping. The ADR then chooses a sequence anyway (lines 52-54).
finding.failure_scenario: 50fc42f is 'plan5i-p3-redo' (part 3 rebuilt on part 2), and the 226 commits interleave p4c-t10c merges into plan5i-p2 and p3-t8 sitting on p2. Without a commit-to-task-to-review map, old review verdicts recorded against the pre-redo commits can be adopted for redo trees they never reviewed. The 'original dispatch order' also cannot be checked against how the history was actually merged.

findings.response: Provide factual 230-row source inventory plus retained actual review/brief evidence; range discovery never implies acceptance.

finding.summary: 'Preserve original dispatch order' is ambiguous because 'T10' names two tasks (Plan4c T10/T10b/T10c and plan5i-2 T10/T10b). The plan5i-2 T10 bridge-flow test was merged as 'strict xfail until T6, T7, T9, T11'.
finding.failure_scenario: The ordering contract cannot tell which T10 must come first. The bridge-flow suite, which the ADR's consumer list requires, may be landed before its prerequisites, or sequenced against the wrong T10.

finding.summary: The harness consumer contract has no concrete mechanism. sensitive_kind flags any 64-hex string as a 'hex key', and harness.py:293 scans json.dumps(composed.ask). The ADR says to 'use the existing approved digest representation' but never names it or what the widened scanner will do with it.
finding.failure_scenario: If the widened scanner (unresolved head) also matches the display digest format, or the ask carries a raw sha256 in the effect, refs or Sources lines, every managed install fails with ASK_UNPOSTABLE. The obvious workaround is the global exemption the ADR forbids, and the design gives no pinned test input to show either way.

findings.response: Pin actual digests functions/format, computed-only callsite trust, full serialized payload tests and human approval for representation changes.

finding.summary: The consumer list was built by grepping for sensitive_kind only. It leaves out wsd/settings.py, a newly present consumer of the scanner module (secret_scan.is_reference and show at settings.py:19-21, 236), and any module that sends text to the relay through notices/asks rather than calling the scanner directly.
finding.failure_scenario: If btq-1wu2i changes show() redaction or is_reference(), settings.py errors and validation change behavior with no 'nonempty actual test selection' recorded for them. That breaks the invariant at ADR line 61 for an unlisted consumer.

findings.response: Include current settings/accounts and indirect native/relay consumers with actual callsite/source pins.

finding.summary: The required consumer suite list leaves out tests/test_wsd_refusals.py and tests/test_wsd_notes.py, even though line 69 requires refusal-reason coverage (asks.py:491 REASON_WITHHELD). Line 96 says 'no skipped required test is a pass' without saying whether the BTQ_REPO-gated test_wsd_beads tests (lines 618, 690) are required.

findings.response: Require refusals/notes plus all seven real-BTQ nodes with honest hosted provenance and skip policy.
